executiveSummary: GM0244 passes the complete deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 12,745 residents, ten neighbourhoods in two districts, one BAG woonplaats, two BRT settlement labels, safety-region assignment, eleven scheduled-transit stop areas and five NWB-derived logical road links are coherent; neighbourhood population differs from the separately rounded municipal control by only ten. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Hattem has a real, locally material IJssel pathway: the LIWO catalogue exposes primary-breach candidate 1103 named Hattem, current HWH geometry identifies primary IJsseldijk sections and the Hoenwaard east/west and outlet defenses, and the Veessen-Wapenveld high-water channel discharges through Hoenwaard back to the IJssel. The model, however, selects none of those events or states while assigning 2.233393 normalized river inundation stress from T+12 through T+72, 7,820 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 and 8,288 at T+72. The exact footprint, ranking, service losses and restoration path must therefore be suppressed as local decision evidence until a named LIWO/water-manager case supplies source water, breach/overtopping and defense assumptions, connected depth/arrival/duration/recession grids and NoData. Eight unrelated hazard families reuse one exact ten-neighbourhood ordering. A controlled source inside the official Hattem5 mixed-forest polygon and Verspreide huizen bosgebied still ranks that source neighbourhood sixth, behind Villapark and low IJssel-side areas. The network also omits the locally important IJsselbrug/Zuiderzeestraatweg bus-and-road approach to Zwolle and Isala, while one generated numeric 050 connector is already signed A50 in its own NWB provenance and remains ambiguously named. Forty-eight public water-register points, one NBNL planning sample, overlapping provider polygons, antennas, schools and external acute care are valuable context, not physical topology or live service state. Static registers, observations, plans and official scenarios must remain distinct from T+72 simulated state; missing data and unselected events never mean zero, absent or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS), Kadaster and PDOK
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Wijken en buurten 2025, full municipal geometry, BAG place and BRT settlement context

supports: Fresh full-resolution feature 0872a895-9526-5e2d-8587-ef9d100dfc71 identifies 2025GM0244 Hattem as a MultiPolygon with 778 coordinate positions and bbox [6.0007883995288935, 52.44376557786849, 6.103545928863948, 52.50960619807545]. The generated centre [6.0521540891122845, 52.474354852965284] lies inside.
CBS OData table 86165NED at https://opendata.cbs.nl/ODataApi/OData/86165NED reports 12,745 residents, density 552/km2, 23 percent aged 65 or older and 1,599 one-person households for GM0244.

The generated regional bundle contains ten official neighbourhoods in two districts. Published neighbourhood cells sum to 12,735 residents, 5,365 households, 1,595 one-person households and 2,945 residents aged 65 or older; the ten-person and four-household-person differences from separate municipality controls are consistent with independent CBS rounding.

One active BAG woonplaats is Hattem; the BRT settlement layer distinguishes Hattem as woonkern and 't Zand as buurtschap. Administrative features are annual/register geography, not flood compartments, live occupancy, utility zones or emergency destinations.

CBS and administrative-boundary data are CC BY 4.0; BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0. Suppressed, unavailable, rounded and not-applicable values retain publisher semantics and are never silently zero-filled.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Hattem with Gemeenten Oldebroek, Elburg, Nunspeet and Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Beleids- en beheerplan Water en Riolering and Hattem implementation context
evidenceSources.edition: adopted December 2020; implementation/model updates described through 2024
supports: The statutory plan treats sewer, transport main, treatment, surface water and groundwater as one interacting chain, while assigning municipal wastewater/rain/groundwater duties and water-board surface-water/treatment duties separately.

Hattem's centre has underground stormwater crates fed from the church roof; the stated purposes are to reduce street runoff, irrigate trees and reduce heat. This is a realized measure, not proof that the whole centre or municipality remains dry in an arbitrary cloudburst.

The municipality's programme page and 2024 budget text at https://www.hattem.nl/dsresource?objectid=51c37825-815c-412d-a6f9-5f82a7a7b8b1&type=pdf say extreme-weather sewer bottlenecks have been mapped with a sewer model completed at the end of 2023 and that some locations require work. Van Lintelweg is an identified water-nuisance project using infiltration crates.

Hattem's Omgevingsvisie at https://www.hattem.nl/dsresource?objectid=367e46da-a68f-499f-a965-cd2ae78cfb75&type=pdf describes the city moat as rain storage, drainage through watercourses/culverts to the polder and a discharge pump to the IJssel. It also identifies the Veluwe-to-river groundwater-fluctuation transition where intense rain can move groundwater toward the IJssel and cause nuisance.

These policy PDFs provide street/system narrative and planned measures but no reusable machine topology, live pump state, compatible capacity units, cell resolution, refresh cadence or explicit standard reuse licence. Their absence fields remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe and Het Waterschapshuis / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: E03 — IJssel/Hoenwaard defenses, Veessen-Wapenveld high-water channel and managed-water registers
evidenceSources.edition: provider-supplied current register queried 2026-09-03; object timestamps vary through 2026-05-05
supports: The bounded public register returns named Vallei en Veluwe sections including primary IJsseldijk dike sections WK-214 Keersluis-Nieuwe Dijk and WK-215 Gelderse Dijk, other defenses Hoenwaard east/west, and outlet dike 't Oever. The bbox also crosses the IJssel and therefore returns defenses managed by Drents Overijsselse Delta; bbox membership is not municipality ownership or hydraulic connectivity.

The water board states at https://www.vallei-veluwe.nl/wat-doen-wij/werken-aan-veilige-dijken/ that the IJsseldijk is a primary defense and that defenses are inspected annually. Register status 'gerealiseerd' or 'vastgesteld' proves an object/register state, not current performance, failure probability or event-time condition.

The official Veessen-Wapenveld page https://www.vallei-veluwe.nl/van-water-genieten/veessen-wapenveld/ says the high-water channel opens at 5.65 m+NAP at Veessen, discharges over the outlet dike into Hoenwaard and rejoins the IJssel at Hattem. It also documents staged gravity/outlet/pump drainage thresholds; those thresholds are system context, not the simulator's current selected forcing.

The deployed HWH snapshot assigns 48 point objects inside full GM0244: 38 weirs, six surface-water pumps, two sluices, one sewer pump and RWZI Hattem. The current project page https://www.vallei-veluwe.nl/actueel/projecten/nieuwbouw-rwzi-hattem/ schedules a replacement RWZI and modified sewer pump through 2028, so planned future capability must not be treated as currently completed.

Keringen/managed-water OGC products are provider-contributed CC BY-SA 4.0 context. Geometry and status are not a connected hydraulic graph; capacities without verified units, controls, power/backup, flow direction and incident state cannot drive exact availability or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — LIWO 2025.1.6 breach catalogue and required flood-scenario semantics
supports: The public WFS bbox returns three primary candidate points; feature id 1103 is explicitly named Hattem, while 3474/3475 are Zwolle Northwest/Southwest and must not be assigned to GM0244 merely because the bbox overlaps them. No regional, regional-water-system or outside-dike candidate point is returned in the same bbox.

The Hattem candidate record exposes opaque breach type, dike-ring and open-water identifiers plus multiple frequency-class flags. A catalogue candidate and flags do not select a breach, probability, defense state, hydrograph or footprint.

IPLO documentation at https://iplo.nl/thema/water/applicaties-modellen/berichtgeving-crisismanagement/liwo/ states that specialist water-management expertise is required. Causal use must pin release, scenario/model date, source-water system, breach/overflow location, defense/control assumptions, variant, native CRS/resolution/units/NoData, depth, velocity, arrival, duration and scenario-clock mapping.

LIWO is an official scenario catalogue, not an observation, warning or forecast. The exact reuse-licence version for the public deployment was not established during this audit; candidate WMS/WFS may remain non-causal scenario-selection context pending licence confirmation.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and incident appendices
supports: The adopted profile covers Hattem within a 22-municipality region and identifies flooding, nature fire, prolonged heat/drought, extreme weather, electricity, drinking water, telecom/ICT and municipal cyber disruption among material crisis scenarios.

The profile describes 25 percent forest/heath and 1.4 million recreational visitors region-wide. For nature fire it says location, wind, terrain, fuel, vulnerable objects, evacuation and scarce specialist capacity materially affect consequences; static combustible-area presence is not an ignition or spread state.

The regional river example is a named Hackfort North dike-break case with a 72-hour pre-breach evacuation start and LIWO consequences. It is not a Hattem calibration, but it establishes that credible flood exercises require a named breach, lead time, footprint and authority decision process rather than generic proximity.

Vitens is identified as the regional drinking-water company, and drinking-water disruption can arise in abstraction, treatment, storage, transport or distribution. Exact Hattem customer bindings, pressure, quality, manual controls and restoration are not published here.

This is strategic four-year risk-planning evidence with no live event API or standard machine-data reuse licence stated. It does not prove current incident probability, resource readiness, utility state or checkpoint completion.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, ProRail, OVapi and Gemeente Hattem
evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB roads, rail/stations, scheduled transit and Hattem transport policy
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01; OVapi feed 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; municipal GVVP published 2018
supports: The generated graph exposes five section-traceable road links: A50 toward Heerde, A28 toward Oldebroek, A28 toward Zwolle, N50 toward Kampen and an ambiguous numeric 050 connector toward Oldebroek. All correctly support only Mobility and explicitly assumed road-logistics Supply in scenario units.

The numeric 050 connector uses source sections NWB-600147118/600147117, whose generated provenance already records signed road number A50, administrative RW50 and road-part class VBD. Retain its geometry as a junction connector but resolve its name/corridor identity rather than showing an unexplained second road 050.

Hattem's GVVP at https://www.hattem.nl/dsresource?objectid=02a32ea4-4caa-4b77-8dde-6326fad531e1&type=pdf identifies the IJsselbrug approach, routes via Geldersedijk/Nieuweweg/Apeldoornseweg, A28/A50 incident diversion through the town and the importance of regional access. Its historic timetable details are not current service.

The current OVapi GTFS snapshot contains eleven in-boundary stop areas, including Hattem IJsselbrug with four grouped platforms. There is no ProRail station in GM0244. RIVM public acute-care context places 24/7 Isala Zwolle approximately 6.51 km straight-line from the municipal reference point, making cross-IJssel/road access an important dependency, not a guaranteed travel time.

The current logical graph does not include the IJsselbrug/Zuiderzeestraatweg local crossing, scheduled bus service, the rail bridge or an explicit route to Isala. NWB is monthly CC0 road geometry, ProRail is CC0 register geometry and OVapi is feed-valid best-effort/free-use schedule context; none proves live passability, service, priority, throughput or destination reachability.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public combustible-nature eligibility at the Hattem/Veluwe edge
evidenceSources.edition: Risicokaart metadata current at retrieval; Hattem source feature valid from 2006-05-24
supports: A bounded WFS request for isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied returns three intersecting mixed-forest polygons from Hattem, Heerde and Oldebroek. Feature Hattem5, identification 0244060066070 and source holder 0244 is the local polygon; bbox intersections from adjacent municipalities must not be silently assigned to GM0244.

The official centre of Verspreide huizen bosgebied [6.042585180530223, 52.45288840785636] is inside Hattem5. A controlled simulator ignition there produces direct fire 0.619640 and smoke 0.569643 at T+24, but ranks the containing neighbourhood sixth of ten behind Villapark, Gelderse Dijk, Hoenwaard, eastern Hattem and De Hilst.

The public layer is eligibility context only. It provides no current ignition, perimeter, fuel load/moisture, visitor presence, wind, smoke transport, access, extinguishing water, crew or suppression state. Its old feature-validity date and missing operational attributes remain visible; no polygon does not mean non-burnable or safe.
The public Risicokaart layer is Public Domain. VNOG's adopted profile supplies process and response relevance but does not turn an eligibility polygon into a current incident.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis, Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RIVM, RDI and DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public utility, care, telecom, education and current-state context
evidenceSources.edition: deployed public-context snapshots 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-03; provider records dated 2025-09-07 through 2026-07-22
supports: A small point bbox around Hattem's reference point returns overlapping electricity polygons for Enexis and Liander and overlapping gas polygons for Enexis, Liander and Stedin; it returns Vitens water, no sewer polygon and nine fixed-media polygons. Provider overlap/no-match must be retained rather than choosing a topology or declaring no service.

The public NBNL sample for postcode 8051KV names OS HATTEM 10-1i and Liander, with withdrawal/injection planning values and 28 projects whose earliest year is 2028. One postcode planning area, congestion classes and future projects are not full-boundary topology, current load, outage, reserve or T+72 restoration.

The deployed public context contains 23 registered antenna installations and nine DUO education locations in GM0244. These are registered equipment/education context, not telecom coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupancy or emergency capacity.

No RIVM surveyed acute emergency department is inside GM0244; Isala Zwolle is nearest in this snapshot and reports 24/7 emergency care, acute obstetrics, 20 treatment rooms and 32,342 2025 emergency visits. These annual questionnaire values do not guarantee incident-time acceptance, staffing, beds or route access.

The cached NDW assignment, RWS Waterinfo, KNMI in-situ and 365-day seismic snapshots have zero GM0244 features. Those are scoped no-match states, not proof that roads are open, water levels/weather are normal, shaking is impossible or the municipality is safe.

Mijn Aansluiting is Public Domain provider-responsibility context; HWH is CC BY-SA 4.0, RIVM care is CC0, DUO registered education is CC BY and RDI terms/cadence are publisher-specific. None supplies safe complete electricity, drinking-water, gas, sewer, telecom, facility, stock or restoration topology.

notes: Peak municipal severities are severe storm 0.683012, pluvial 0.574044, river 0.696221, coastal 0.011628, heat 0.663554, winter 0.673085, cyber 0.521121, earthquake 0.100709, wildfire 0.164030 and compound 0.945173.

River T+72 holds 2.233393 inundation stress, pressure 0.601561, 8,288 affected and 490,763.300 cumulative event-attributable person-hours. Compound T+72 holds 0.562676 flood stress, pressure 0.671749, 9,549 affected and 541,442.265 person-hours.

Coastal direct flood is exactly zero but generic wind/service effects accumulate 11,347.539 person-hours by T+72. This can remain a narrow coastal-screen result only; it is not an all-water all-clear or evidence of an actual coastal event affecting Hattem.

notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0244 pnpm audit:model passed one test file and both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 30.57 seconds.
Every zero-intensity preset gives exact zero current/peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; values are finite/bounded; causal ledgers close; cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic; and route flow stays within effective scenario capacity.
Every local detail has ten rows summing to 12,745 allocated residents; all eight local demand and delivery totals reconcile within floating-point tolerance.
Changing selected map/service layer leaves municipality and neighbourhood hazard values invariant, and current NWB links appear only under Mobility and Supply.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers close, but the scenario does not select Hattem's breach, defenses, access decisions, resources or operator actions.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service baselines plus deltas sum to availability and weighted service losses sum to municipal pressure.
Cumulative person-hours reconcile against a no-event local pre-network counterfactual and are model-equivalent unmet essential-service burden, not observed outage hours or named victims.

No trace records LIWO candidate/scenario selection, water level, dike inspection/failure, Hoenwaard state, evacuation/vertical-shelter decision, IJsselbrug/A28/A50 passability, Isala acceptance, pump/utility isolation, stock delivery or restoration clearance.
Compound exposes an empty unsupportedDimensions array although no local rain, wind, flood, cyber target or service topology is selected.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound plateaus and other exact recovery curves lack measured recession, access, repair resources and checkpoint evidence.
notes: River forcing and seven service values remain exactly fixed from T+12/T+24 through T+72; Facilities falls further by T+48 and then freezes. Persistent high water can legitimately block restoration, but no selected Hattem hydrograph, compartment or defense state establishes this plateau.

Compound rain and wind fall to zero by T+72, yet flood stress stays 0.562676 and all service values freeze from T+48 to T+72 while affected population remains 9,549. No dewatering, bridge inspection, access, crew, material, generator, telecom, hospital, shelter or stock action explains this state.
Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, earthquake and wildfire also expose exact restoration trajectories without operator commitments or event-valid observations.

A defensible first-72-hour trace should explicitly gate: T-72/T+0 scenario and defense confirmation; T+0–6 warning/contact and Hoenwaard/bridge/route checks; T+6–12 evacuation or vertical-shelter decision; T+12–24 utility/RWZI protection and alternate care/supply access; T+24–48 measured recession/dewatering and inspections; T+48–72 owner-cleared staged restoration. Planned projects never auto-activate.

findings.summary: Hattem's 2025 identity, full boundary, region, neighbourhoods, places and demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 confirms full feature 0872a895-9526-5e2d-8587-ef9d100dfc71, the in-boundary centre, 12,745 residents, ten neighbourhoods and one BAG place. Neighbourhood population is only ten below the separately rounded municipal control and the engine allocates back to the control.
findings.action: Retain source edition/retrieval, full-versus-generalized geometry, published-versus-allocated totals, rounding/suppression rules and explicit null semantics on every refresh.

findings.summary: Genuine IJssel exposure is converted into unsupported exact local river consequences without selecting a Hattem event or defense state.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 establish primary IJsseldijk and Hoenwaard defenses, the Veessen-Wapenveld discharge pathway and LIWO primary candidate 1103 Hattem. Current river output nevertheless fixes 2.233393 normalized stress from T+12 through T+72, reports 7,820 affected at T+24 and 8,288 at T+72 and publishes exact service/recovery values without scenario ID, source-water hydrograph, breach/overtopping state, connected depth/arrival/duration/recession grid or NoData.
findings.action: Retain Hattem's river-eligible classification and generic amplitude only as an internal non-operational diagnostic. Suppress decision-facing inundation percentage, neighbourhood rank, affected count and dependent service/recovery precision until a water-manager-selected, versioned LIWO case supplies scenario/model dates, source water, breach/defense/control variant, footprint, depth, velocity, arrival, duration, recession/dewatering and uncertainty. Keep pluvial, groundwater, sewer and other local water pathways separately Unknown—not safe/zero.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one exact ten-neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Villapark first, Gelderse Dijk second and Hoenwaard third, followed by the same seven areas. No LIWO grid, sewer/terrain surface, wind exposure, heat surface, cyber boundary or fire geometry determines this order.
findings.action: Replace the shared municipality seed with hazard-family-specific eligible domains and event-valid surfaces. Add GM0244 unsupported notes now, preserve NoData, and regress that unrelated hazard families cannot silently reuse a complete local ordering.

findings.summary: A controlled ignition inside official Hattem forest does not control local fire allocation.
findings.evidence: The controlled source [6.042585180530223, 52.45288840785636] lies inside IPO Hattem5 and Verspreide huizen bosgebied. It produces direct fire 0.619640 and smoke 0.569643 at T+24, but the source neighbourhood ranks sixth behind Villapark, Gelderse Dijk, Hoenwaard, eastern Hattem and De Hilst. The canonical source is remote and produces zero local flame.
findings.action: Require an explicitly named ignition/perimeter intersected with versioned combustible land cover, fuel/moisture, event-valid wind/smoke, people/recreation, access, extinguishing water and suppression state. The source domain must lead direct exposure unless a documented physical model explains otherwise; no selected ignition remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Exact pluvial consequences ignore Hattem's local sewer, moat, polder, groundwater and pump pathways.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies a 2023 sewer model, local bottlenecks/Van Lintelweg works, centre storage, moat/culvert/polder discharge and the Veluwe-to-IJssel groundwater transition. The preset instead reports 0.545752 stress, 2,446 affected and drainage 0.408150 at T+24 using the same rank as seven unrelated hazards and none of those systems.
findings.action: Obtain the governed municipal 2023 sewer-model/stress-test export with rainfall case, terrain, buildings, sewer/culvert/pump assumptions, native resolution, units, version, licence and NoData. Until then retain national/regional rain maps as non-causal context and suppress local depth/rank/affected precision.

findings.summary: The model omits the IJsselbrug/Zuiderzeestraatweg access dependency to Zwolle and publishes an ambiguous numeric 050 connector.
findings.evidence: E06 and the current GTFS identify the IJsselbrug approach and grouped stop, while the nearest surveyed 24/7 acute hospital is Isala Zwolle across the IJssel. None of the five logical edges represents the local IJsselbrug, bus continuity or destination route. Separately, nwb-link-430 is named 050 although its own provenance says signed A50/RW50 and class VBD.
findings.action: Retain the five source-resolved road geometries only for Mobility/Supply. Resolve 050 to the verified A50 junction-connector identity without adding duplicate capacity, and add a separately audited IJsselbrug/Zuiderzeestraatweg crossing from current NWB/BGT geometry with bridge/passability state Unknown. residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete, safe and current physical electricity, drinking-water, gas, sewer, telecom, facility or emergency-supply topology for GM0244; provider polygons and road geometry cannot substitute for it.
LIWO candidate 1103 is a catalogue location, not a selected breach, probability, forecast or depth footprint; specialist scenario selection and deployment-licence confirmation remain required.

HWH defense/water-object registers are provider-contributed and partial. Realized/fixed status does not establish hydraulic connectivity, performance, current operation, compatible capacity, control, power/backup or restoration.

The municipal 2023 sewer model/stress test, detailed catchments, culverts and pump controls are not available as a governed reusable machine dataset in this audit; policy descriptions cannot be rasterized into invented precision.
The Hattem5 polygon is old-validity combustible-area eligibility only. Current fuel/moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/smoke, people, access, extinguishing water and suppression remain Unknown.

NWB/ProRail/GTFS are static geometry or scheduled context. IJsselbrug, A28, A50, N50, rail and buses require event-valid passability/service/priority data; zero NDW assignment is not proof of open access.
RIVM acute-care values are annual questionnaire context. Isala Zwolle's route, acceptance, staffing, beds and backup during the exercise remain Unknown.
CBS residents omit workers, visitors, pupils, patients, passengers and responders at incident time. Annual or scheduled counts must not be divided into invented T+hour occupancy.

Exact model service availabilities, affected resident-equivalents, scenario-unit capacities, preparedness, reserves and person-hours are exercise constructs and must not be described as observations, forecasts, probabilities, victims or operator commitments.
No-match, null, outside-boundary, transparent raster and incomplete provider fields remain typed Unknown/NoData. They never mean zero, absent, normal, open or safe.
